title: I almost gave up on my game showcase, but people kept submitting their games
author: An4rcyst
selftext:
I built this small site where people can share the games they’re making. I was excited about it at first, but after spending more time looking around, I started getting discouraged.

There are already so many places to discover games. So many directories, communities, websites with much bigger audiences. Every time I found another one, I had the same thought: why would someone use mine?

I didn’t really have a good answer. I still don’t have a complete one.

So I haven’t talked about the project much lately. I left it online, but I was starting to question how much more time I should put into it.

Today I went through the submissions. There were 19 new ones waiting since my last check, bringing the total to over 30.

I spent some time opening the links, looking at screenshots, watching gameplay and reading what people had written. There were little browser puzzles, management games, mobile games, unfinished projects looking for feedback.

Some people had written a few lines. Others had explained their game in detail and what they wanted people to try. Reading those made me feel a bit bad about how quickly I’d started dismissing my own project. They had taken the time to put their work on it while I was sitting there wondering whether the site was worth continuing.

I checked Google Search Console too. Between October 7 and 17, the site had around 6,000 impressions and 200 clicks. The numbers are small, but I was happy to see it starting to show up in searches.

The submissions meant more to me, though. I got to spend part of today looking at things people had made, then helping them put those things in front of someone else. That was the part I’d been excited about when I started.

I still need to figure out how to bring players back and give these games useful attention. Having developers submit doesn’t solve that, and I know there’s a lot left to do.

But I finished going through the queue feeling more motivated than when I opened it. I wanted to work on the site again.

I thought I’d share that, because most of the updates I see are about big launches or impressive numbers. Mine is just that a few people used something I made, and it helped me get past a week of wondering why I was making it.

That felt nice. I’d spent so much time thinking about what the site was missing that I hadn’t really stopped to appreciate that people were actually using it.

I still don’t know where it’ll go, but it made me want to keep working on it.

I built it with Codex. The idea is to give each game its own space, where the creator can share gameplay and updates, ask for feedback or playtesters, and let people follow its progress.

It’s free to use, and games don’t need to be finished or made with AI.

There’s still a lot to improve, especially getting players to come back, but seeing people share what they’re making feels like a good start.

[postyourgame.com](http://postyourgame.com)
